title: Finite principal-support vanishing assembles the specified derived open unit
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and for every scheme $W$ put $\Lambda_W=p_W^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules on the small pro-etale sites [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], their ordinary unbounded derived categories, total derived direct images and the specified derived adjunctions [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}S$ be affine, $r\geq0$, $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in S$, and $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})$. For $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ put $X_J=X[1/\prod_{b\in J}f_b]$, $K_J=K|_{X_J}$, and $i_J:X_J\hookrightarrow X$. For $a\notin J$ let $d_{a,J}:D_{a,J}=V(f_a)\hookrightarrow X_J$, with complementary principal open $e_{J,a}:X_{J\cup\{a\}}\hookrightarrow X_J$. Define $R\underline\Gamma_{D_{a,J}}$ as the right derived functor of $M\mapsto d_{a,J}^*\ker(M\to e_{J,a,*}e_{J,a}^*M)$ [det-lem-formal-closed-support-adjunction]. Assume
$$R\underline\Gamma_{D_{a,J}}(K_J)=0\quad\text{for every }J\text{ and }a\notin J.$$
Then the actual adjunction unit $\eta_J:K\to R(i_J)_*i_J^*K$ is an isomorphism for every $J$. Under the comparison $R(i_{J\cup\{a\}})_*\cong R(i_J)_*R(e_{J,a})_*$ conjugate to canonical pullback composition, its unit satisfies
$$\eta_{J\cup\{a\}}=R(i_J)_*(\eta_{e_{J,a},K_J})\circ\eta_J.$$
Thus every ordering of a finite set gives the same specified unit, with the empty-set unit the identity under the canonical identity-functor comparisons. All isomorphisms are in the derived category, including when $K=0$, $X$ is empty, $r=0$, or some indicated closed subschemes are empty.

proof.text: All restrictions in the statement are the specified module pullbacks. By [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main] they are exact for this arbitrary commutative condensed $\Lambda$. The exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] identifies their left derived functors with termwise restriction. Thus the specified adjunctions of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] read $i_J^*\dashv R(i_J)_*$ and $e_{J,a}^*\dashv R(e_{J,a})_*$ on the ordinary unbounded internal-module derived categories, and $K_J=i_J^*K$ with the canonical restriction comparisons.

source.place: Exactness statement; exact-functor and adjunction conventions in sk-def-sfb-derived-categories and sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull

proof.text: Fix $J$ and $a\notin J$. The open $e=e_{J,a}$ is quasi-compact: for any affine open $W\subset X_J$, its inverse image is the principal affine open $D(f_a|_W)$ of $W$. Apply [det-lem-formal-closed-support-adjunction](4) on $X_J$ with $d=d_{a,J}$ to obtain the distinguished triangle $d_*R\underline\Gamma_{D_{a,J}}K_J\to K_J\xrightarrow{\eta_{e,K_J}}Re_*e^*K_J\to(d_*R\underline\Gamma_{D_{a,J}}K_J)[1]$. Its first object is zero by the assumed vanishing (the additive $d_*$ sends zero to zero). Rotate this triangle using [def-weil-triangulated-category]: the third object of the rotated triangle is zero. The criterion [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] therefore proves that the actual unit $\eta_{e,K_J}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Clause (4), with Stacks derived.tex Tag 05QR, label lemma-third-object-zero, after rotation

proof.text: Put $i=i_J$, $e=e_{J,a}$ and $h=i_{J\cup\{a\}}=ie$. By [prop-sfb-module-left-derived-upper-star-comp], the canonical restriction comparison is $Lh^*\cong Le^*Li^*$. Conjugate its inverse by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] to obtain $Rh_*\cong Ri_*Re_*$, exactly the comparison stipulated in the item. Here is the unit identity explicitly: for adjunctions $L_1\dashv R_1,L_2\dashv R_2$ and $\tau:L_2\xrightarrow{\sim}L_1$, substitute the defining formula for $\tau^c$; naturality of $\eta_2$, naturality of $\tau$ and then $R_2$ applied to the triangle identity $\varepsilon_{1,L_1K}\circ L_1(\eta_{1,K})=1_{L_1K}$ give $\tau^c_{L_1K}\circ\eta_{1,K}=R_2(\tau_K)\circ\eta_{2,K}$. Take $(L_1,R_1)=(Lh^*,Rh_*)$ and $(L_2,R_2)=(Le^*Li^*,Ri_*Re_*)$. The unit of this latter composite adjunction is $Ri_*(\eta_{e,i^*K})\circ\eta_{i,K}$ by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. After the canonical target restriction comparison, the displayed identity is precisely $\eta_{J\cup\{a\}}=R(i_J)_*(\eta_{e_{J,a},K_J})\circ\eta_J$. This proves equality of the specified maps, not merely existence of some isomorphism between their targets.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, label lemma-derived-pushforward-composition (conjugation by the pullback comparison); categories.tex Tag 0DV0, label lemma-compose-counits, and the explicit conjugate-unit calculation

proof.text: For $J=\varnothing$, the canonical identification $X_\varnothing\cong X$ identifies restriction with the identity. Under [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] the identity adjunction has identity unit. Conjugate the identity comparison on the left adjoint by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. The unit identity calculated in step 3 then says that the specified unit for $i_\varnothing$ becomes $1_K$ under the canonical right-adjoint comparison. In particular $\eta_\varnothing$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0DV0, label lemma-compose-counits; identity adjunction and conjugation, specialized unit calculation of step 3

proof.text: Induct on the cardinality of $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$. The base is step 4. If $J\ne\varnothing$, choose $a\in J$ and set $I=J\setminus\{a\}$. Then $|I|<|J|$ and $a\notin I$. The hypothesis of the item and step 2 give invertibility of $\eta_{e_{I,a},K_I}$; the induction hypothesis gives invertibility of $\eta_I$. A functor carries an inverse to an inverse, so $R(i_I)_*(\eta_{e_{I,a},K_I})$ is invertible. Step 3 identifies their composite with $\eta_J$, which is therefore invertible. This covers every subset $J$, rather than only initial segments of one ordering.

source.place: Agent finite induction from Tag 0D6E, label lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, using steps 2–4

proof.text: For any ordering of a finite subset, start with the unit of step 4 and apply the equality of step 3 at each insertion. Induction on the length of this list identifies its composite with the one fixed morphism $\eta_J$. Two orderings hence give equal morphisms after the stipulated comparisons, without selecting cone isomorphisms. The argument permits $r=0$ and $K=0$. If $X$ or some $X_J$ is empty, all constructions still take place in the corresponding module derived category. If a closed complement is empty, step 2 has zero first term; if a principal open is empty, the same triangle and the assumed support vanishing force $K_J=0$. Thus no nonemptiness, regularity or non-zero-divisor hypothesis on the $f_a$ was used.
